## Open

### T-633 — The suite database needs its schema, then its admin

> _2026-11-10 · suite/blong-suite · open_

blong-suite exists in the dev MySQL with no tables: the suite was once deployed with a MySQL of its
own, which was removed, and it now points at the shared instance while its pods read a database
nothing has created. A proper redeploy should let the migrate and fill jobs create the schema under
the release intent, after which the operator's own account (admin) has to be created there too,
because the release seeds declare roles and capabilities but no users.

## Done

### T-600 — The blong namespace has no process or path in the suite

> _2026-11-02 · suite/blong-suite · done_

The `blong` namespace has no process and no ingress path in this suite, so its pages are drawn but
unserved. The browser bundle carries the realm (the Observe menu comes from it), the plan's realms
are `core`, `access`, `marine` and `login`, and the generator writes `/rpc/<deployment>` only for a
deployment named after its namespace; `POST /rpc/blong/flow/find` through the portal host therefore
falls to `/`, reaches the portal's pod and answers `connect ECONNREFUSED 127.0.0.1:9455`. Decide
which way: give the realm a process and a path (`blong: {}` in the `k8s`, `upgrade` and `release`
realm lists, which adds a fifth pod), or drop the Observe pages from this suite's menu. Verify with
the proxy: `blong-dev proxy --port 8097 --target https://marine.feasible.one` then
`POST /blong/flow/find`.

Implemented as D-833: the realm declares itself attached to core, so the plan writes its layers onto
that deployment, labels the pod for the blong namespace, publishes services/blong.yaml and routes
/rpc/blong there; the monolith needs no case of its own. A deployment still has no semantic-log
service to point the adapter at (T-645).
